t: Flat white - Wikipedia
s: January 16, 2026 - A true flat white ought to have the same quantity of extracted coffee as any other beverage on the coffee menu (generally 30 ml; 1.1 imp fl oz) but because it is served in a smaller vessel (175 ml; 6.2 imp fl oz) it has stronger flavour than say a latte which is normally served in a 225 ml (7.9 imp fl oz) vessel and is subsequently milkier. The consistency of the milk is another point of difference between a flat white and a latte – a latte has a creamy, velvety layer of milk on the surface which can vary in depth depending on where you buy your coffee.
